title: Rational normal curve in its own linear span
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $n,e\in\mathbf N$, and $i:Y\to\mathbf P^n_k$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Say that $i$ is a rational normal curve of degree $e$ in its own linear span if $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $e>0$, the space of restricted linear forms has dimension $h_i(1)=e+1$ [def-sfb-projective-coordinate-hilbert-polynomial], and there is a $k$-isomorphism $\alpha:\mathbf P^1_k\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ with $(i\circ\alpha)^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n}(1)\cong\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}(e)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. The dimension clause says the embedding in its span uses the complete degree-$e$ system: $h^0(\mathbf P^1,\mathcal O(e))=e+1$.

source.place: Morrison §3.2, Theorem 8 proof step (3), printed p.14; Gieseker Proposition 1.0.3, pp.30--31. Complete linear-system meaning explicitly specified by lem-sfb-component-projection-weight-bounds and lem-sfb-integral-curve-span-degree-rigidity.
